metadata.description: Year-by-year carbon accounting for monoculture rubber vs rubber agroforest over 100 years
metadata.sign_convention: negative = sequestration/removal from atmosphere, positive = emission to atmosphere
metadata.cumulative_sign: negative cumulative = system has been net sink overall

sources.mono_biomass_model: Logistic growth model from Thailand GHG study (ScienceDirect 2013). Peak ~128 tC/ha.
sources.mono_peak_stock: CIFOR-ICRAF SE Asia review (Agus et al.) — time-averaged 56 Mg C/ha; peak ~128 tC/ha
sources.clearcut_residue: IPCC 2019 root:shoot ratio 0.246 for tropical moist Asia; wood product retention 40% from literature
sources.clearcut_pulse_duration: 3-year decomposition window (standard IPCC assumption for harvest residues)
sources.n2o_baseline_fertilized: Scientific Reports 2016 — 4.0 kg N-N2O/ha/yr fertilized rubber plantation, Xishuangbanna
sources.n2o_spike_clearcut: ~3x baseline for 2 years post-clearcut due to soil disturbance + heavy replanting fertilization
sources.ch4_sink_unfertilized: EGUsphere 2025 — unfertilized rubber soil CH4 sink -2.9 kg CH4/ha/yr
sources.ch4_fertilized: EGUsphere 2025 — fertilized: sink reduced 60% to -2.1 kg CH4/ha/yr
sources.ch4_heavy_fert: EGUsphere 2025 — heavy fertilization transforms to net source +0.3 kg CH4/ha/yr
sources.agro_biomass_ceiling: CIFOR-ICRAF — rubber agroforest 176.6 Mg C/ha aboveground + IPCC BGB ratio
sources.agro_sequestration_rate: Nair et al. 2009 (ScienceDirect) — tropical agroforestry 4.85 tC/ha/yr biomass + 2.23 tC/ha/yr soil
sources.agro_soil_ceiling: ScienceDirect 2025 global meta-analysis — mean soil C stock agroforestry 159.1 Mg/ha
sources.agro_n2o: Scientific Reports 2016 — unfertilized rubber 2.5 kg N-N2O/ha/yr
sources.soil_degradation: PLOS One 2013 (Yunnan, SE Asia analog) — forest-to-rubber soil C loss ~0.81 tC/ha/yr over 46 yrs

caveats: No 100-year empirical study of rubber agroforest exists. Agroforest values projected from documented stock data and regional rates.
Soil carbon in monoculture modeled conservatively at -0.5 tC/ha/yr; actual losses may be higher per PLOS One 2013.
Clearcut pulse assumes 3-year decomposition. Some studies suggest 5-7 years for stumps/roots.
N2O clearcut spike (3x, 2 years) is an estimate; direct measurements of replanting N2O pulse are limited.
CH4 values are small relative to CO2 and N2O — included for completeness but do not materially change argument.
Wood product carbon (40% of AGB) treated as locked for the 100-yr window. In reality ~50% is released within 50 yrs.
